summary.intent: Backfill missing Phase 47 SUMMARY.md files, run Phase 48 verification, and implement the missing API endpoint needed to persist encrypted share itemName during lazy backfill.
summary.outcome: All three tasks completed: Phase 47 summaries backfilled via agent, Phase 48 VERIFICATION.md written via agent, and a new PATCH /shares/:shareId/item-name endpoint was built (DTO, service method, controller, specs, client regeneration, web wiring re-enabled) with 171 tests passing and web typechecks clean.

repo: The GSD resume-incomplete invariant checks SUMMARY.md count vs PLAN.md count on disk — it trips as a false positive when code shipped via PR but summaries were never written to disk (Phase 47 shipped via PR #494 / commit d17d42e5f with a complete VERIFICATION.md but zero SUMMARY.md files).
Phase 48 had a BLOCKED-HANDOFF for bin-restore e2e failures (REQ-1) that predated PRs #500 and #504 which resolved it — handoff files can be stale after subsequent PRs land.
The web-side backfillSentShareItemNames was fully implemented but commented out inside fetchAllSentShares, waiting on a PATCH endpoint that never existed in the API.
@Patch(':shareId/encrypted-key') served as the exact structural analog for the new @Patch(':shareId/item-name') endpoint — same auth guard, same service delegation pattern, same DTO shape.
pnpm api:generate bumps the OpenAPI spec version (0.38.0 → 0.39.0) in every generated file header on each run — this is expected regeneration noise, not meaningful changes.
.planning/intel/ is untracked by git and should be excluded from commits.
The shares domain has 171 tests covering the controller and service layers.

code.finding: itemNameEncrypted was computed and then voided (not persisted) at this site — the missing persist call was the root cause of the lazy backfill gap.
New DTO file created; mirrors UpdateEncryptedKeyDto structure with itemNameEncrypted field and matching validation.
New updateShareItemName method added immediately after updateShareEncryptedKey — follow this placement convention for future share mutation methods.
New @Patch(':shareId/item-name') endpoint added adjacent to @Patch(':shareId/encrypted-key') — both follow the same guard/auth/delegation pattern.
Barrel export file must be updated manually when adding new DTOs — not auto-discovered.
Generated client function for the new endpoint lands here after pnpm api:generate — verify presence before wiring web imports.

workflow: When GSD --next would mechanically route to a destructive action (re-execute a phase that already shipped), verify via git log before acting — git history and VERIFICATION.md are more authoritative than SUMMARY.md presence.
Running pnpm api:generate is required after any API endpoint addition; without it the web TypeScript imports will reference non-existent generated functions.
The web app has no dedicated typecheck npm script — run tsc directly against the tsconfig or use the build command to validate types.

Dispatching bookkeeping tasks (summary backfill, verification write) to parallel agents while doing substantive implementation work in the main thread is an effective parallelization pattern for this GSD workflow.
Committing in two logical commits (feature vs. planning bookkeeping) keeps the git history clean when a session mixes implementation with documentation work.

friction: gsd_run query roadmap.analyze returned empty plan counts, forcing a manual directory scan to detect incomplete phases.
The GSD resume-incomplete invariant produced a false positive that would have re-executed already-merged work — the mechanical --next route had to be overridden based on git history investigation.
The web app lacks a typecheck npm script, requiring direct tsc invocation to validate types.
api:generate produces pre-existing warnings on every run, making it harder to spot real new issues in the output.
open_items: Legacy shares already in production will only get their itemName backfilled on next fetchAllSentShares call — no bulk backfill mechanism exists for existing shares.
Phase 47 SUMMARY.md files are now backfilled (cosmetic) but the root cause — sessions completing execution without writing summaries — is not addressed upstream.
Phase 48 VERIFICATION.md was written but the original BLOCKED-HANDOFF for bin-restore e2e (REQ-1) should be reviewed to confirm the handoff file was cleaned up.
The feature branch commit was staged at end of transcript but final confirmation of push/PR creation was not shown — may need a PR opened.
No integration or e2e test covers the full lazy-backfill round-trip (fetchAllSentShares → backfillSentShareItemNames → PATCH item-name → encrypted at rest).
